### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. neurodevelopmental disorder with alopecia and brain abnormalities  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.436)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-351202)

**Proposed mechanism:** SMS (HGNC:10979) —DISRUPTS→ spermidine metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1907986); ODC1 (HGNC:7970) —DISRUPTS→ spermidine metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1907986); spermidine metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1907986) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); spermidine metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1907986) —LEADS_TO→ Alopecia (HP:0001049); spermidine metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1907986) —LEADS_TO→ Brain abnormalities (HP:0002084). Loss-of-function mutations in SMS (disease A) and ODC1 (disease B) both disrupt the critical pathway of spermidine metabolism, leading to a shared downstream consequence of intellectual disability, alopecia, and brain abnormalities.

**How to falsify it:** If variants in SMS and ODC1 are found at a high frequency (>1%) in gnomAD populations and are not significantly enriched in patients with these disorders, or if experimental evidence demonstrates that the dysregulation of spermidine metabolism does not causally link to the observed phenotypes. _(variant: HGNC:10979,HGNC:7970)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of spermidine metabolism in these distinct neurodevelopmental disorders could reveal common therapeutic targets. Interventions aimed at restoring spermidine levels or modulating its metabolic pathway might offer a unified treatment strategy for both syndromic X-linked intellectual disability Snyder type and neurodevelopmental disorder with alopecia and brain abnormalities.
